documents.title: BrightPath Community Grants Policy 2025-2026
BrightPath Community Grants Policy 2025-2026
documents.content:
**4. Application Procedures**

4.1 **Application Period.** Applications for the 2025–2026 cycle open on 2025-08-01 at 09:00 hours (Singapore time). The application deadline for BrightPath Community Grants is 2025-10-31. Record status: current. This deadline is current and will not be extended. Applications must be received by the Grants Operations Office by 23:59 hours on the deadline date. Any application received after this time will be considered late and will not be assessed.

4.2 **Application Form.** Applicants must complete the official BrightPath Community Grants application form. The form is available for download from the BrightPath website (www.brightpath.org.sg/grants) or may be requested by email from grants@brightpath.org.sg. The form must be completed in full. Incomplete forms will be returned to the applicant for resubmission, provided the resubmission is received before the deadline.

4.3 **Supporting Documents.** The following documents must be submitted together with the application form:

- A copy of the applicant organisation's constitution or rules;
- A copy of the group's most recent financial statement (if available);
- A detailed project proposal, including objectives, target beneficiaries, and implementation timeline;
- A project budget, itemising all expected income and expenditure;
- A letter of support from the organisation's advisor or a relevant community leader (for groups without formal registration);
- A copy of the venue booking confirmation or a letter of intent from the venue owner (if the venue has been identified);
- A completed risk assessment form (template provided with the application form).

4.4 **Submission Method.** Applications may be submitted by email to grants@brightpath.org.sg or by post to:

Grants Operations Office
BrightPath Community Grants
c/o BrightPath Centre
15 Lorong 3 Geylang
Singapore 388591

For emailed applications, the subject line must read "BrightPath Application – [Organisation Name] – [Project Title]". Attachments should be in PDF format. The Grants Operations Office will send a confirmation of receipt within three working days. If no confirmation is received, the applicant should contact the office by phone (6123 4567) or email.

4.5 **Acknowledgement of Receipt.** Each application will be acknowledged by email or post. The acknowledgement will include a unique application reference number. Applicants should quote this reference number in all subsequent correspondence with the Grants Operations Office.

4.6 **Late Applications.** Applications received after the deadline will be marked as "late" in the application register. Late applications will not be considered for funding in the 2025–2026 cycle. No exceptions will be made, except where the delay was caused by a failure of the Grants Operations Office's own systems. In such cases, the applicant must provide evidence of the system failure, such as a timestamped email delivery report.

4.7 **Withdrawal of Application.** An applicant may withdraw their application at any time before the Letter of Award is issued. Withdrawal must be made in writing, by email or post, to the Grants Operations Office. The application reference number must be quoted. A withdrawn application will be removed from the assessment queue, and any supporting documents will be returned to the applicant or destroyed, at the applicant's request.

4.8 **Change of Contact Details.** Applicants must notify the Grants Operations Office of any change in their contact details (postal address, email address, or phone number) during the application period. Failure to do so may result in missed communications regarding the application.

documents.content:
(b) **Community need** – the clarity of the identified need and the strength of the evidence provided for that need, including any data, surveys, or consultations cited in the application;

(c) **Project design and feasibility** – the logic of the project plan, the realism of the timeline, the qualifications of the project team, and the adequacy of the budget;

(d) **Sustainability** – the likelihood that the project's benefits will continue after the grant period ends, and the plan for continued funding or community support; and

(e) **Value for money** – the reasonableness of the requested grant amount relative to the expected outcomes and the number of beneficiaries served.

Each criterion will be scored on a scale of 1 to 5, with 5 being the highest. A total score will be calculated, and the Panel will also record brief comments on each criterion. The Panel will meet at least once per assessment round. The Panel may invite applicants to a clarification session if the written application leaves material questions unanswered. Clarification sessions will be held by video call or in person at the BrightPath Centre. No new information may be introduced during a clarification session; the applicant may only clarify what was already in the application.

5.4 **Stage Three: Award Decision.** Following the technical review, the Grants Operations Office will prepare a shortlist of applications for final decision. The final decision will consider the Panel's scores and comments, the availability of funds, and the overall balance of the portfolio of awards across different priority areas and applicant types. The target number of awards for BrightPath Community Grants is 20. Record status: current. The Grants Operations Office will aim to make up to 20 awards in the 2025–2026 cycle, subject to the quality of applications and the availability of funds. If fewer than 20 applications meet the quality threshold, fewer than 20 awards may be made. If more than 20 applications meet the quality threshold, the highest-scoring applications will be selected, and the remaining applications will be placed on a reserve list in score order.

5.5 **Reserve List.** Applications placed on the reserve list may be offered an award if a selected applicant declines the award or is unable to accept it. The reserve list will be valid until 31 March 2026. Applicants on the reserve list will be notified of their status in writing. They may be contacted at any time up to that date if a place becomes available. No appeal is possible against the decision to place an application on the reserve list rather than to select it for an award.

5.6 **Equal Treatment.** All applications will be assessed on their merits, without regard to the applicant's race, religion, gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, or political affiliation. The Grants Operations Office will keep a record of the assessment scores for each application for a period of three years after the end of the cycle, for audit purposes.

5.7 **Confidentiality.** All information provided in applications will be treated as confidential. The Grants Assessment Panel and the Grants Operations Office will not disclose the content of any application to third parties, except as required by law or with the written consent of the applicant. Panel members will be required to declare any conflict of interest with respect to an application, and will recuse themselves from the discussion and scoring of that application.

documents.content:
**BrightPath Community Grants Policy 2025-2026**

**Part 8: Project Reporting and Conditions**

8.1 **Reporting Obligations.** A grantee must submit to the Grants Operations Office the following reports in respect of a funded project:

(a) an interim progress report, due no later than the date stated in the grant agreement, which shall describe the activities carried out to date, the outputs achieved against the milestones in the approved work plan, and any significant deviation from the work plan;

(b) a final project report, due within 60 days after the project completion date stated in the grant agreement, which shall describe the project outcomes, the outputs delivered, the number of beneficiaries served, and lessons learned; and

(c) a financial report, due together with the final project report, which shall set out the actual expenditure of grant funds against the approved budget, with supporting receipts and other documents as specified in the grant agreement.

8.2 **Report Format.** All reports must be submitted in the format prescribed by the Grants Operations Office from time to time. Reports may be required to be submitted through the online grant management system. Where a grantee is unable to submit a report electronically, the grantee may request, in writing, permission to submit the report in hard copy.

8.3 **Certification by Authorised Signatory.** Each report must be certified by the authorised signatory of the grantee organisation, or by the umbrella organisation's authorised signatory where the grant is held by an umbrella organisation under section 7.2. The certification shall confirm that the information in the report is true, accurate, and complete, and that the grant funds were used only for the purposes of the project.

8.4 **Site Visits and Inspections.** The Grants Operations Office, or any person authorised by it, may carry out site visits, inspections, and audits of a grantee's premises, records, and project activities. The grantee must provide all reasonable access and assistance for this purpose. Site visits may be announced or unannounced.

8.5 **Records to be Kept.** A grantee must keep, for a period of at least five years from the date of the final report, full and proper records relating to the project, including:

(a) financial records, including invoices, receipts, bank statements, and payroll records;

(b) records of project activities, including attendance lists, photographs, and publicity materials;

(c) correspondence with the Grants Operations Office; and

(d) any other records that the Grants Operations Office may reasonably require.

8.6 **Acknowledgment of Support.** A grantee must acknowledge the support of the BrightPath Community Grants programme in all publicity materials, publications, and other outputs arising from the funded project. The form of acknowledgment will be specified in the grant agreement. A grantee must not use the BrightPath name or logo in any way that suggests endorsement of the grantee organisation or its activities beyond the funded project.

8.7 **Conditions on the Use of Funds.** Grant funds must be used only for the approved project and for the budget items set out in the approved budget. A grantee must not, without the prior written approval of the Grants Operations Office:

(a) transfer grant funds between budget lines where the transfer exceeds 10% of the total grant amount;

(b) use grant funds for any capital expenditure exceeding $5,000 per item;

3. Primary activity alignment
   - The grant's objective is community food security, including food distribution, community gardening, nutrition education, and reducing food waste. The project proposal focuses on digital literacy for seniors. While the proposal mentions that workshop participants will be taught to use online grocery delivery platforms and food donation apps, the primary activity is not aligned with the grant's stated objective of community food security. The proposal does not include any food-related activities such as meal preparation, food growing, or food distribution. Criterion not met.

4. Prior grant compliance
   - No prior CFRG grant. No outstanding reporting obligations. The applicant has not received any other public grant in the current financial year. Satisfactory.

5. Target beneficiary profile
   - The grant prioritises projects serving low-income families, vulnerable seniors, and residents of public rental housing. The application states that beneficiaries are seniors aged 60 and above residing in Tampines, without specifying income criteria. The proposal does not include a mechanism to verify beneficiary eligibility or prioritise low-income participants. Criterion not met.

6. Supporting documents
   - All required documents received by 30 Oct 2025, including the signed declaration, the society's certified accounts for FY2024, and the project proposal (18 pages, within the 20-page limit). The declaration was signed by the society's secretary on 29 Oct 2025. However, the certified accounts for FY2024 were prepared by an external auditor but were not accompanied by the auditor's opinion letter. The accounts were accepted provisionally pending the opinion letter, which was not received by the screening date. Criterion not fully met.

7. Budget and financial capacity
   - Proposed budget: S$48,500. The budget includes S$12,000 for workshop materials (tablets and SIM cards), S$8,000 for venue rental, S$15,000 for trainer honoraria, S$6,000 for refreshments, and S$7,500 for administrative costs. The refreshment cost of S$6,000 appears high relative to the number of workshops proposed (48 sessions). No breakdown of refreshment costs was provided. Criterion not met.

**Status definitions.**
- *Eligible* – applicant meets all screening criteria as of the screening date. Status is current unless subsequently revised.
- *Ineligible* – applicant does not meet one or more criteria. Status is current unless subsequently revised.
- *Pending* – screening incomplete; additional documents or clarifications requested.
- *Superseded* – a previous determination has been replaced by a later review of the same applicant for the same grant cycle.

**Screening criteria (summary).** (1) Registered society or charity in Singapore; (2) at least one year of operating history; (3) project serves residents of a town covered by the Fund; (4) no outstanding grant reporting obligations to the Fund or other public agencies; (5) governance documents in order; (6) financial statements submitted; (7) budget reasonable and aligned to proposed activities.

Screening is performed by a Grants Officer and countersigned by the Assistant Director. Where a criterion is not met, the specific gap is noted in the Remarks column. Applicants are notified by email and registered post.
